YouDot · Internship Case Study
Blogger Studio
Redesign.
Redesigning the core editor and admin dashboard for YouDot's blogging platform — addressing a 38% publishing abandonment rate through deep usability research and systematic UI overhaul.
Role
Product Design Intern
Platform
Web SaaS
Year
2025
The Problem
A 38% publishing abandonment rate
Users would open the YouDot editor, begin writing, and stop before hitting publish. Not because they changed their mind about the content — but because the interface was getting in the way. The product team knew something was wrong but couldn't pinpoint where.

"Users couldn't locate the publish action — it didn't match their mental model of a content tool. They expected it near the title, not buried in a toolbar they'd never scrolled to."

Research Method
10 moderated usability sessions
I ran 10 moderated sessions with YouDot users — a mix of casual bloggers and professional content creators. Each session followed a structured task script: draft a post, add formatting, save a draft, and publish. I recorded every hesitation, mis-tap, and verbal comment.
Root Causes Found
Three problems, not symptoms
Session analysis exposed three distinct root issues: (1) The editing and publishing states were visually indistinguishable — users couldn't tell if they were in "draft mode" or "publish mode". (2) No autosave feedback created low-level anxiety, causing tab hoarding. (3) The toolbar had zero visual hierarchy — formatting, saving, and publishing competed with equal weight, making the most important action invisible.
Solution — Smart Editor
Two redesigned products shipped
I delivered two complete redesigns: the Smart Editor and the Blogger Admin Dashboard. The editor introduced a clear Draft/Publish state split, a persistent autosave indicator in the top bar, and a reorganised toolbar with strong action hierarchy. The admin dashboard gave editors and admins full visibility of content performance, writer activity, and pending actions — all in one dark-themed operational interface.
Editor improvements
Publish CTA always visible — top-right, distinct colour
Persistent autosave indicator in header — zero anxiety
Toolbar hierarchy: formatting → insertions → publish
Page Contents panel — quick navigation for long posts
SEO panel accessible from editor — no context switching
Before
62%
task completion rate
After
97%
task completion rate
Dashboard Design
Admin visibility,
finally done right.
The admin dashboard gives content managers a real-time operational view — live blog stats, writer activity, pending approvals, and quick actions — all in a dark, high-contrast interface designed for daily use on large monitors.
📊
Real-time blog stats
Total blogs, published count, drafts, and pending items shown as live metric cards — each with trend indicators and status labels.
👥
Writer activity feed
Active/idle writer status, latest contributions, and quick action menus — keeping editors and admins aligned without constant check-ins.
⚡
Quick actions panel
One-click access to create post, approve all pending, and generate reports — the three most frequent admin actions surfaced to the top.

Fynxx · Internship — Three Projects
Three clients.
Three worlds.

At Fynxx I worked across three very different product contexts — maritime, fitness, and food — each demanding a completely distinct visual identity and user mental model.

Fynxx · Project 01
HeyPorts
A shore leave platform for maritime crews — helping sailors navigate unfamiliar ports safely. Find local services, book transport, get safety alerts, connect with crewmates, and discover local culture during brief port stays.
Platform
Web + iOS App
Users
Maritime Crews
Year
2026
The Challenge
Helping sailors navigate the unknown
Maritime crews arrive at unfamiliar ports for 12–48 hour windows. They don't know local safety conditions, transport options, currency exchange rates, or where their crewmates are. Language barriers and limited data add further friction. The challenge was building something that worked offline, across cultures, in high-stress moments.
Key Design Decisions
Safety-first information hierarchy
The app opens to a live city dashboard with the crew's current port, local recommendations, and safety alerts immediately visible. Shore services (restaurants, pubs, sight-seeing, cab booking) are surfaced in a scannable grid. The SOS button is always reachable — never buried. Crew discussion enables real-time coordination. Scan-at-facility enables premium service access without friction.
Web Landing Page
Dual audiences, one page
The landing page serves both crew members and port operators. A bold hero with the city name and live shore leave trends establishes immediate relevance. The feature set unfolds in alternating light/dark sections — shore trends, local currency, reliable transit, health warnings — ending with a coming-soon countdown and emergency SOS CTA.
🧭
Shore Services
Restaurants, pubs, sight-seeing, and cab booking — all accessible from the home screen grid.
🆘
Emergency SOS
Always-accessible SOS button connecting crew to emergency services and port authority in under 10 seconds.
💬
Crew Chat
Real-time discussion channel for crew members at the same port — coordinate meetups, share tips.
📍
Port Map
Offline-capable map with marked safety zones, facilities, and curated local landmarks.
Fynxx · Project 02
Hourly Gym
A gym discovery, booking, and session tracking app for fitness-first urbanites who want flexible access across multiple studios — pay per session, not per month. Built with a high-contrast dark aesthetic designed for performance-focused users.
Platform
iOS Mobile App
Theme
Dark / High-contrast
Year
2026
The Challenge
Flexible fitness without commitment anxiety
The traditional gym model — long contracts, single location — doesn't fit how urban fitness enthusiasts actually train. They want to try CrossFit on Monday, yoga on Wednesday, and a pool on Saturday. Hourly Gym needed to make multi-gym discovery, comparison, and session booking feel effortless — not like managing multiple memberships.
Key Screens Designed
Dashboard, Explore, Compare, Map
The dashboard leads with the active session timer — for users mid-workout — and transitions to weekly intensity stats and nearby studios. The Compare screen is the product's standout feature: select up to 3 gyms, see a side-by-side rating, tier, distance, and specialty breakdown, then book the winner in one tap.
Visual Direction
Performance-grade dark UI
Deep black backgrounds with red accents signal performance and intensity. Real gym photography in cards makes discovery visceral, not abstract. Typography is heavy and condensed — every element feels like it was built for someone who takes fitness seriously.

Fynxx · Project 03
Coffee App
A specialty coffee ordering app — immersive onboarding, curated product discovery, and a warm two-toned aesthetic that balances a dark moody hero with a clean light browse experience.
Platform
iOS Mobile App
Theme
Dark hero + Light browse
Year
2025
Design Direction
Two moods, one product
The design leans into a deliberate two-mode feel. The onboarding screen is full-bleed, dark, and editorial — a cinematic coffee photograph with dramatic steam and falling beans sets an emotional tone of richness and indulgence. The moment the user enters the app, the palette flips to warm light tones with a clean product grid — switching from mood to utility seamlessly.
Key UX Decisions
Browse built for discovery
The home screen opens with a promo banner (BOGO offer), then a horizontally scrollable category filter (All Coffee, Machiato, Latte, Americano), and a product grid with photograph-first cards showing rating, name, type descriptor, and price with an add button. Location context is shown in the header — important for a delivery app. The navigation bar stays simple: Home, Wishlist, Cart, Notifications.
☕
Immersive Onboarding
Full-bleed photography with dramatic lighting sets the product's emotional tone before the first tap.
🏷️
Promo Banner System
Prominent BOGO offer card increases order value and engagement on first browse session.
📍
Location-Aware Header
City and neighbourhood shown at top — critical context for a delivery service operating across multiple areas.
⭐
Rating-First Cards
Rating badge overlaid on product photo — the first thing a user scans when choosing between similar items.
Personal Project · Case Study
Nectar
Grocery Delivery
Designing an end-to-end grocery delivery experience for a modern, time-strapped urban user — from first open to confirmed order.
Role
Lead UI/UX
Platform
iOS
Year
2024
Problem
Grocery apps fail at the moment of purchase
Cluttered discovery, no persistent cart total, and a checkout experience that revealed delivery time only after payment — a trust-breaking late reveal that caused drop-off.

"I just want to find my usual items fast and get out. Why is this harder than the actual store?"

Persona
Priya, 29 · Working professional, Bangalore
Shops on phone during commute. Wants her weekly staples in under 10 minutes. Trusts an app that shows delivery time before asking for her card details.
Flow
Delivery time shown before payment
Key insight from testing: showing the delivery window before checkout was the single highest-impact trust moment. Everything else was iteration — this was the insight that changed the sequence.

Fashion eCommerce
100+ screens across 8 complete user journeys — from account creation to order delivered — for a style-conscious audience who shops with intention.
Role

Screens

Open in Figma →
The Tension
Discovery vs. conversion
Fashion shoppers browse emotionally but abandon logically. The tension between inspiring discovery and frictionless checkout is where most fashion apps fail. I needed both — not a tradeoff.

"Users want to feel like they're in a boutique, but checkout must feel like their bank — fast, safe, familiar."

Wishlist vs. Cart
Clear mental model, reduced abandonment
Separating "save for later" from "buying now" with distinct UI patterns removed the confusion that caused most mid-session drop-offs in early testing.

📦 Order tracking & returns

Personal Project · Case Study
Task Manager
& To-Do App
Progress-first design that shows what you've done, not just what's left. Built around reducing cognitive load, not adding to it.
Platform
iOS
Theme
Soft Pastel
Year
2024
Insight
Apps that show your failures, not your wins
Most task managers open to a list of undone tasks. I wanted to flip that — design an app where every interaction highlights progress made, creating a reinforcing sense of momentum rather than guilt.

"The app should feel like a supportive colleague, not a demanding manager."

Visual Language
Calm by design
Soft pastels on white, generous spacing, circular progress indicators that feel satisfying rather than pressurising. The 3D illustrated onboarding character sets a warm emotional tone before the user has created a single task.
